To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the airflow induced by door opening and human passage through the doorway of isolation rooms is affected by the door type, the ventilation rate, and the flow differential.

(1) The airflow pattern through the doorway of an isolation room is strongly affected by the door type, (2) the door opening motion itself generates a greater air volume transfer across the doorway than healthcare worker passage, and (3) the airflow through the doorway can be significantly reduced by a flow differential between supply and exhaust.

1) hinged door opening generates greater flow across the door opening than sliding door, 2) ventilation rate has only a small effect in the air exchange across the door opening with the hinged doors, and 3) supply-exhaust flow differential reduced the door opening induced airflow, and 4) the human passage induced substantial air exchange across the isolation room doorways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of isolation room doors that are effective at containing airborne pathogens.
understanding the airflows induced by the operation and passage of single hinged/sliding isolation room doors and how they affect the air exchange through the doorways.
the airflow patterns through single hinging and sliding doors in negative pressure isolation rooms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sliding door design is the preferred choice for isolation rooms.

the sliding door is the best choice for isolation rooms, because it has the smallest air exchange across the doorway when the door is opened, and it also has the smallest air volume transport across the doorway when healthcare workers walk in and out of the room.
sliding door should be preferred over the hinged one in negative pressure isolation rooms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the airflow patterns in isolation rooms are highly dependent on the door type and the ventilation system configuration.
the door type should be considered as an additional design parameter for the isolation room ventilation system.
the sliding door should be used in isolation rooms to minimize the risk of cross-infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of the isolation room doorway type is important to reduce the risk of cross-infection, and that the design of isolation room doorways should be based on a detailed understanding of the airflow patterns induced by door opening and passage.
the door type should be selected carefully in order to reduce the risk of cross-infection in hospital isolation rooms.
